name: Who wrote it? — famous opening lines
description: Match a famous opening line to its public-domain novel. Every line is a verbatim excerpt (not a paraphrase or a widely-circulated 'quote about reading', which are frequently misattributed) — the same lines used on the /learn sample site's library dashboard.

source.name: Public-domain novels (Austen 1813, Melville 1851, Dickens 1850/1859, Tolstoy 1878, Shakespeare c. 1599) — text verified against the works themselves.

items.question: "It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune must be in want of a wife." — who wrote this opening line?
items.explain: It's the opening line of Pride and Prejudice (1813).

items.question: "Call me Ishmael." is the famous opening of which novel?
"It was the best of times, it was the worst of times..." opens which novel?
items.explain: Charles Dickens published A Tale of Two Cities in 1859.

items.question: "All happy families are alike; each unhappy family is unhappy in its own way." opens which novel?
items.explain: Leo Tolstoy published Anna Karenina in 1878.

items.question: Which author wrote: "All the world's a stage, and all the men and women merely players"?
items.explain: The line is from Shakespeare's As You Like It, spoken by the character Jaques.

items.question: "Whether I shall turn out to be the hero of my own life... these pages must show." opens which Dickens novel?
items.explain: Charles Dickens published David Copperfield in 1850, earlier than A Tale of Two Cities.
